status: PERMANENT REQUIREMENT — concepts only; environments not implemented
scope: All 100 missions, with immediate design requirements for Campaign 1 Arcs 2–5

existingState.playable: Missions 1–10 only; all belong to Arc 1. Later arcs are an authored archive, not playable environments.
existingState.currentReuse: World.jsx shares market landmarks between 3/6, wrecks between 4/9/10, and towers between 5/7/8. This is existing Arc 1 content and is not a template for later arcs.
existingState.layout: Current worlds largely use a shared ground plane and road progression. Future arcs require separately authored topology and route graphs.
existingState.archiveCaution: Mission 12 currently repeats the Glass Wastes title/description. Preserve the archive entry pending narrative review; do not copy Mission 2 terrain, formation placements or encounter layout into Arc 2.

rules: Preserve mission IDs, order, purposes, story decisions, characters, unlock rules and saved progress.
An unlabelled gameplay screenshot must identify the arc through geography, structural silhouettes and atmosphere, not HUD text or recoloring.
Each arc owns its terrain, architecture kit, landmarks, level topology, sky/weather/lighting, palette, hazards and interactive vocabulary.
Do not reskin a prior map, reuse building arrangements or substitute decorations for new architecture.
Share engine systems, shaders, generic material utilities and invisible technical components; do not share the defining map or architecture silhouettes across arcs.
Environment mechanics must support existing mission purposes; all concepts below are proposals, not new canonical events.
Within-arc progression may revisit its own landmarks with authored changes. Story-required continuity at arc boundaries may show a distant earlier landmark without recycling the playable map.
Keep Ashwatthama's meaningful, gradually revealed Arc 4 role in Missions 31–40. Do not insert him into Mission 5.

concepts.name: Complex & Yaskin
concepts.geography: An elevated enclosed logistics belt attached to the Complex: deep service shafts, suspended freight decks and controlled interiors rather than Kashi streets.
concepts.architecture: Radial pressure bulkheads, ribbed monocoque shells, sealed bridges, monumental lift cores and recessed surveillance galleries. New kit, no Kashi tower blocks.
concepts.terrainAndVegetation: Machined decks, coolant conduits and restricted hydroponic service bays; engineered greenery only where supply infrastructure justifies it.
concepts.skyWeatherLighting: Sky glimpses through high apertures; pale glare outside, cool controlled lighting within; ventilation condensation rather than desert dust.
concepts.palette: Bone ceramic, graphite, restrained clinical cyan and warning amber.
concepts.routesAndLandmarks: Radial loops around a freight-lift spine, stacked crossovers and concealed maintenance bypasses; a suspended intake crown as the principal silhouette.
concepts.hazardsAndInteractions: Timed freight crossings, lift interlocks, surveillance sightlines and coolant isolation controls; clearly telegraphed safe routes.
concepts.encounterDirection: Security patrols, drones and shielded checkpoint formations supporting infiltration, freight sabotage, escapee protection and stolen-identity missions.
concepts.withinArcEvolution: Exterior supply approach to restricted processing galleries and outer-ring access, retaining authored mission purposes. Mission 12's glass motif, if retained, requires a new industrial topology.

concepts.name: Sumathi & the Pursuit
concepts.geography: A peripheral Kashi drainage basin opening into wind-cut frontier escarpments, braided dry channels and a contested border crossing.
concepts.architecture: Low rammed-earth shelter compounds, corrugated wind screens, cable ferries and repurposed conduit safehouses; no stacked city blocks or Complex shells.
concepts.terrainAndVegetation: Eroded sediment banks, loose scree, dry channels and sparse thorn scrub with vegetation concentrated at sheltered water traces.
concepts.skyWeatherLighting: Wind-driven dust fronts, wide overcast skies and a progression toward the existing dusk crossing; visibility changes must be readable during pursuit.
concepts.palette: Chalk ochre, faded indigo fabric, rust red and muted storm blue.
concepts.routesAndLandmarks: Braided escape routes, alternate shelter loops, ridge bypasses and a narrow border-span landmark. City scenes use this peripheral basin identity without changing their Kashi setting.
concepts.hazardsAndInteractions: Searchlight exposure, dust-reduced sightlines, unstable scree and reversible decoy gates; safehouse doors and escort routes support the existing pursuit narrative.
concepts.encounterDirection: Tracking parties, mixed hunter ambushes and mobile interdiction squads. Protecting Sumathi and choosing an escape route remain the mission purposes.
concepts.withinArcEvolution: Crowded peripheral shelter lanes gradually give way to exposed channels and the frontier crossing; no reused Arc 1 street layouts.

concepts.name: Shambhala & Ashwatthama
concepts.geography: A concealed stepped mountain valley with a river, misted ravines, terraced refuge paths and sheltered cliff chambers.
concepts.architecture: Hand-cut stone buttresses, timber galleries, woven shade structures, water channels and inhabited rock sanctuaries; no industrial city kit.
concepts.terrainAndVegetation: Wet rock, river gravel, moss, hanging roots, riparian reeds and carefully tended terrace vegetation.
concepts.skyWeatherLighting: Broken cloud, river mist, cool dawn shafts and an authored night-defense treatment; warm inhabited interiors contrast with the valley exterior.
concepts.palette: Jade, weathered limestone, deep teal water and restrained warm ochre lamps.
concepts.routesAndLandmarks: Vertically braided footpaths, river evacuation branches, cliff overlooks and a concealed water-gate silhouette. Separate layouts for approach, sanctuary, river passage and outer defenses.
concepts.hazardsAndInteractions: River current, wet ledges, sluice controls, defense signals and concealed access mechanisms, each introduced with readable collision and camera clearances.
concepts.encounterDirection: Protective cooperation, scout interception, evacuation defense and night perimeter encounters. Ashwatthama's trust, oath and protective purpose shape existing missions without an immediate full reveal.
concepts.withinArcEvolution: Hidden approach to lived-in sanctuary, river evacuation and threatened outer perimeter. Preserve gradual anticipation and the established oath chapter.

concepts.name: The Awakening
concepts.geography: The exposed outer defense escarpment beyond Shambhala, opening into a fractured basalt ravine and ash-covered frontier plateau. Do not replay the Arc 4 valley map.
concepts.architecture: Angular emergency earthworks, broken causeways, huge exposed geological ribs and sparse siege structures; sanctuary continuity appears only as distant context where required.
concepts.terrainAndVegetation: Black columnar rock, fractured passes, scree, ash deposits and isolated scorched scrub. No lush valley terraces.
concepts.skyWeatherLighting: Heavy storm canopy, directional breaks of light, drifting siege ash and controlled lightning accents. Mythic memory sequences use authored spaces tied to existing revelation missions.
concepts.palette: Basalt black, ash grey, copper embers and restrained pale-gold revelation light.
concepts.routesAndLandmarks: Defensive cross-lines become collapsing-pass evacuation routes and broad last-stand arenas; a split basalt crown and severed causeway define the skyline.
concepts.hazardsAndInteractions: Telegraphed falling debris, breached defenses, controllable barricades and evacuation chokepoints. Destruction should use bounded authored states rather than uncontrolled expensive simulation.
concepts.encounterDirection: Coordinated siege forces, defensive holds and survivor protection supporting the already-authored breach, ravine, last stand and awakening sequence.
concepts.withinArcEvolution: Pressure at the outer defenses, evacuation through new ravine geography, then existing memory and revelation events. Do not move revelations earlier or resolve Ashwatthama's arc prematurely.

remainingArcs.policy: Apply the same uniqueness gate to every remaining arc before implementation. These directions preserve the current archive and remain proposals.
remainingArcs.6: A New Dawn: repairable frontier waterworks and irrigated settlement terraces, distinct from Arc 3's dry escape basin and Arc 5's basalt siege terrain.
remainingArcs.7: The Far Frontier: tidal salt sea, submerged archive access, reef-like industrial wreckage and weather-driven flats; unique tidal routes.
remainingArcs.8: The War of Cities: multiple fortified free-city plazas, civic bridges and siege corridors with independently authored urban plans, not Kashi tier blocks.
remainingArcs.9: The Celestial Engine: subterranean astronomical vaults, crystalline machinery and hollow-mountain chambers with spatial puzzle routes, not a recolored Complex.
remainingArcs.10: The Next Era: rebuilt New Kashi civic terraces and public transit spines; maintain distant historical continuity while authoring new playable geography and buildings.

implementationGates: Before new runtime work, inspect the current campaign entries, mission scripts and environment implementation again; document how each proposed layout serves the existing objectives.
Author a separate terrain/topology and architecture kit per arc, with independent collision and navigation layouts. Do not route later mission IDs through the existing Arc 1 world as a substitute.
Review unlabelled gameplay screenshots for geography, architecture silhouette, terrain and lighting identity; color alone cannot pass.
Test keyboard, joystick, solid/sensor contacts, camera clearance, encounters and all mission interactions in the new layouts.
Stream only the active mission/arc. Batch repeated components within each unique kit, use LOD and bounded texture budgets, and budget shadow casters and transparent overdraw.
Measure matched production frame times and GPU queries on AMD integrated graphics, including the densest view and combat. Treat 60 FPS as a target until measured, not as a promise.
Do not start this environment implementation by rewriting completed missions or delaying the unfinished Phase 2 character, camera and reliability acceptance work.
